article_title: Cline CLI 3.0.71 loads plugins inside its hub instead of a separate node or bun process and adds a cline hub plugins command

content_preview.title: Cline CLI 3.0.71 loads plugins inside its hub instead of a separate node or bun process and adds a cline hub plugins command
content_preview.summary: Cline's CLI v3.0.71 release notes say plugins now load inside the hub, so no JavaScript runtime is needed on PATH, and describe a new cline hub plugins status command.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cline's command-line agent has a new plugin loading model. According to the [CLI v3.0.71 release notes](https://github.com/cline/cline/releases/tag/cli-v3.0.71), "Plugins now load inside the hub instead of a separate node or bun process, so the CLI no longer needs a JavaScript runtime on your PATH to run plugins." GitHub's release timestamp for the tag is 08:56 UTC on October 13, 2026.

editor_notes.content_quality: Tight News item of 658 words (raw and with link URLs stripped; News range 400-1200). Title is 124 characters (cap 150). Structure is clear: lead with the verbatim release-note sentence, a section on the failure-visibility changes, a list of the other 3.0.71 changes, the SDK v0.0.93 release, context from 3.0.70, and a candid 'What We Don't Know' section. Every claim is attributed to Cline's own release notes and the article says so, including that no independent testing was done.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots source-0, source-1 and source-2 (.html.gz) all exist, status 200, and each contains the full release-notes body (div body-content), not page chrome only; suspicious_patterns is null for all three. source-0 (cli-v3.0.71): the title's first claim is verbatim: 'Plugins now load inside the hub instead of a separate node or bun process, so the CLI no longer needs a JavaScript runtime on your PATH to run plugins.' The quoted sentence ends at 'plugins.' in the source, so the quote is complete. The second claim is supported: 'the new `cline hub plugins` shows each plugin's status and last error (`--reload <plugin>` re-imports one without restarting the hub)'. The notes say 'new' but do not use the word 'command'; calling it a command is a fair description of a CLI invocation. Also confirmed: warning naming plugin and error, `cline config tools --json` lists a `plugin_failure` entry, CLINE_PLUGIN_MODE=sandbox keeps the old subprocess behavior, and every bullet in the 'other changes' list (--thinking in ACP mode, cline hook agent_error, OPENROUTER_API_KEY counting as configured, first model in the recommended list = Claude Sonnet 5.5, reasoning off on every provider, image token estimate, scheduled-run fixes, symlinked rule files, .claude/skills). source-1 (sdk/sdk/v0.0.93): the quote 'Plugins load in-process through one registry per process instead of a node/bun subprocess, so the compiled CLI and its hub no longer need a runtime on PATH.' is verbatim up to PATH, but the source sentence continues ', and plugins can use the Bun global under the Bun-built hub.' The article ends the quote with a period inside the marks. The omitted clause is an additive detail and does not change the meaning of the quoted portion, so this is recorded as a concern, not a correction. State list loading/ready/degraded/failed/disabled with last error, per-session module copies, and CLINE_PLUGIN_MODE=sandbox keeping the subprocess sandbox all confirmed. source-2 (cli-v3.0.70): 'cline dashboard is now cline hub dashboard. The old command still works as a hidden alias' and the 'unknown option' removal of `cline history --page` (with 'Remove them from scripts') confirmed; the quoted phrase 'unknown option' is verbatim. Dates verified in the snapshots AND through the GitHub releases API (not any summarizer): cli-v3.0.71 published 2026-10-13T08:56:25Z; sdk/sdk/v0.0.93 published 2026-10-13T08:26:52Z (earlier the same day, as the article says); cli-v3.0.70 published 2026-10-08T05:55:09Z. All 2026; the article states 08:56 UTC and October 13, 2026, and October 8, 2026, correctly. No WebFetch was needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated specifics found. The inference about the CLI and SDK wording is clearly labelled in the article ('The matching wording suggests a connection, but that is an inference, not something either set of notes states') and is not stated as fact. Editorial observation: the SDK note itself mentions 'the compiled CLI and its hub', so the SDK note is closer to the CLI change than the article's 'nearly identical wording' phrasing conveys; the wording is similar, not identical, but the claim made is hedged and acceptable. One imprecision: the summary says the notes 'describe a new cline hub plugins status command'. The notes describe a command named `cline hub plugins` that shows plugin status; they do not name a 'status' subcommand. The title and body are accurate; only the summary is ambiguous. Filed as a clarification.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Vendor claims are attributed ('the notes say', 'according to the notes', 'the maintainers' wording'). No AI self-reference, no promotional language.
editor_notes.originality: Archive search for Cline (word match across src/content/articles and submissions): the only prior Cline coverage is 2026-02/23 (prompt-injection supply-chain attack on the Cline CLI), plus incidental mentions in a Red Hat Summit piece and a Nous Research Hermes piece. No article covers Cline CLI releases, so the article's statement that no other article covers them holds. Related curated links added to the meta file: the Feb 2026 Cline supply-chain article and the OpenCode 1.19.0 article (new plugin API).
concerns: Summary says 'a new cline hub plugins status command'; the release notes name the command `cline hub plugins`, which shows status, and no 'status' subcommand. Clarification filed.

SDK quote is closed with a period after PATH, but the source sentence continues ', and plugins can use the Bun global under the Bun-built hub.' Omitted clause does not alter the meaning; no correction required.
'Nearly identical wording' for the SDK and CLI notes slightly overstates the match; the claim linking them is correctly labelled as inference.
Source snapshot check: the writer's WebFetch summary reportedly gave year 2024; the article uses 2026, matching both snapshots and the GitHub API, so there is no date error.
recommendations: When a summary names a command, reproduce it exactly as the source does and put any description of what it does outside the command name.
When quoting a sentence that continues in the source, end the quote before the period or add an ellipsis.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed, correctly sized article resting on three primary release pages whose full bodies were read. Approved with one clarification on the summary wording.
